display.purpose: Page title only; 2rem below sm, 2.5rem from sm; text-wrap balance.

headline.purpose: Prose h2, opened by a hairline rule with 2rem padding (none when first).

lead.purpose: Page description under the title, muted, max 60ch.

body.purpose: Prose at 88% foreground; running text held to a 38rem measure.

label.purpose: Breadcrumb, contents entries, card descriptions; sidebar links at 14px.

label-section.purpose: Sidebar group titles, On this page, table headers; sentence case.

code.purpose: Code blocks; inline code at 0.84em weight 500; ligatures off.

shadows.name: lift
shadows.purpose: Hover state of link cards and previous/next cards, with a 1px rise.

shadows.name: rest-whisper
shadows.purpose: Code frames and the search trigger at rest.

motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: Exponential ease-out for every enter and positional transition.

motion.name: marker-slide
motion.purpose: Contents marker and tab indicator sliding to the active item.

motion.name: dialog
motion.value: in 260ms var(--ease-out) from translateY(8px) scale(0.98) blur(2px), out 140ms ease-in

motion.name: drawer
motion.value: in 320ms var(--ease-out) from translateX(-100%), out 180ms ease-in

motion.name: menu
motion.value: in 180ms var(--ease-out) from scale(0.96) translateY(-4px), out 120ms ease-in

motion.name: article-crossfade
motion.value: old 120ms ease-in fade-out, new 280ms var(--ease-out) from translateY(6px)
motion.purpose: View transition on page change; shell stays put.

motion.name: reading-progress
motion.purpose: Header progress hairline; hidden without scroll-timeline support.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.value: durations collapse to 0.01ms; view transitions none

narrative.overview:
**Creative North Star: "The Exact Reference Desk"**

The category standard played straight: a quiet reading column set inside a crisp three-column shell (sidebar, article, contents rail), built for a developer with an editor and terminal open beside it. Code is the primary content, so code frames get the most deliberate chrome on the page and prose stays calm around them. Density is moderate: generous line height in prose, tight 13 to 14px wayfinding text in the rails.

Every neutral carries a faint violet tint (hue 286) so the single .NET violet accent reads as part of the page rather than pasted on. The accent marks location, links and focus, and nothing else. Depth is mostly tonal and hairline; real shadows are reserved for layers that float above the page. Motion is short, exponential ease-out, and exists to keep the reader oriented: the contents marker slides, the jumped-to heading flashes, the article crossfades on page change. All of it drops to none under reduced motion.

The build rejects the stock template look: flat gray neutrals, default borders, no motion, no wayfinding beyond the sidebar.
keyCharacteristics: Violet-tinted neutrals with one violet accent, in light and dark themes.
Inter for UI and prose, JetBrains Mono for code, with ligatures off.
Hairline (1px) rules everywhere; 12px radii on code frames, cards, tables and callouts.
Translucent sticky 56px header with backdrop blur and a scroll-driven reading-progress hairline.
Wayfinding on every page: sidebar pill, breadcrumb, sliding contents marker, previous/next cards.

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Violet is spent on location, links and focus. It never fills a large surface; the only solid violet fills are the brand tile and the 2px progress and tab indicators.

rules.name: The Tinted Neutral Rule
rules.body: No pure gray. Every neutral sits at hue 286 with chroma between 0.002 and 0.014.

rules.name: The One Tone Per Job Rule
rules.body: A callout derives its ground, hairline and icon from a single status token so both themes stay in step.

rules.name: The Sentence Case Rule
rules.body: Labels and group headings are sentence case at normal tracking. No uppercase tracked labels.

rules.name: The Literal Code Rule
rules.body: Code ligatures are always off; what a reader sees is what they paste.

rules.name: The Float-Only Shadow Rule
rules.body: A visible shadow means the element sits above the page or is responding to the pointer. Static content containers never carry more than the rest whisper.

rules.name: The Glass Header Rule
rules.body: The header is translucent with a strong backdrop blur and saturation, so scrolling content stays faintly visible beneath it.

dos: Do keep every neutral on hue 286 at low chroma, and define both a light and a `.dark` value for any new token.
Do reserve violet for location, links and focus; mark the current place in every navigation element with it.
Do frame code, tables, tabs, callouts and cards with a 1px hairline and a 12px radius.
Do use the Float shadow only for dialogs and drawers and the Lift shadow only on hover of interactive cards.
Do animate with the exponential ease-out (`cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1)`) at 150 to 320ms on enter, faster ease-in on exit, and let `prefers-reduced-motion` collapse it to none.
Do keep running text at a 38rem measure and let code and tables use the full column.
Do give every copy action visible and announced feedback.
donts: Don't use pure grays or untinted borders.
Don't add shadows to static content containers beyond the rest whisper.
Don't put uppercase tracked labels or small accent-coloured kickers above headings; group labels are 12px semibold sentence case.
Don't fill large surfaces with violet or introduce a second accent hue; status hues live only in callouts and feedback.
Don't exceed weight 600 in the docs surface.
